actionThatDiffers: Switch straight to the one pane that matters instead of cycling eight tabs reading each scrollback to identify it.
why: Claude Code already generates session titles and terminal tab titles usually carry the repo or task; per session it is on screen or one glance away, so access is low. Impact is real but small: it only saves seconds of tab-cycling, it does not change which work gets done.

actionThatDiffers: Review findings get recorded against the workflow gate instead of living only in one session scrollback the user must re-read later.
why: This is something the user DOES: type one prompt into the first-officer session or run the spacedock CLI, so 21-40 per the action rule. Impact is narrow - only Spacedock users have gates at all, and the fallback (paste the findings into the gate yourself) is cheap. Briefing says nothing here, hence low confidence.

actionThatDiffers: Undo or restore immediately after a force-push, reset --hard, rm, or schema write, instead of discovering the damage days later when the reflog window has passed.
why: No harness reports this and a pane sweep only shows the visible tail, so recovering it means reading transcripts across every session and back in time - the classic 61-80 correlation case. Deciding which actions count as irreversible is a heuristic classification, so the value rests on the detector being right. Impact is genuine loss prevention.

actionThatDiffers: Re-steer or kill a session that has drifted off the goal I gave it, and spot two sessions doing the same work, instead of letting both run to completion.
why: Each session holds its own goal in its own pane, so a tmux capture-pane loop yields an adequate approximation of all of them - the loop rule caps this at 60. It is above 40 because the goal is often far up the scrollback and has to be reconstructed. Impact changes a real steering decision fairly often.

actionThatDiffers: Go straight to the one session that is blocked or finished, instead of sweeping every pane every few minutes; blocked sessions stop sitting idle for twenty minutes unnoticed.
why: No harness offers a cross-harness view, but tmux list-panes plus capture-pane, backed by ps for GUI harnesses, gives an adequate approximation in one pass, so the loop rule holds it at or below 60. Impact is the highest on this board: idle blocked sessions are the concrete wasted hours, and this is what changes attention allocation all day.

actionThatDiffers: Restart a trivial docs or test-fix session on a cheaper model after seeing it sitting on the expensive one, preserving quota for the session that needs it.
why: Most status lines print the model unprompted and /model shows it otherwise; sweeping panes composes the per-session values, and per the composite rule an arithmetic roll-up of individually visible inputs cannot outrank them. Impact is a real recurring decision but not a loss-prevention one - the work still completes on the expensive model.

actionThatDiffers: Stop or throttle the one runaway session that is eating the window, rather than stopping everything or riding into the cap and losing the rest of the afternoon.
why: The inputs are not individually visible, so the composite cap does not apply: quota is shown only as a single global current figure, no harness attributes consumption to a session, and /context gives size not rate. Getting a per-session burn rate means sampling transcripts over time across sessions - real correlation work. Impact protects a quota window, which is concrete loss.

actionThatDiffers: Stop re-checking a session I already dealt with, so the next sweep only shows things that are actually outstanding.
why: This is an action, and the equivalent today is one keystroke: close the tab, kill the session, or just move on - so 21-40. Impact is board hygiene: it makes the surrounding view trustworthy but no work outcome changes, and it only matters at all once you already have the board.

actionThatDiffers: Start the next task on the harness that still has headroom instead of on the one about to cap, avoiding a hard stop mid-task and a wait for reset.
why: Claude /usage and the Codex usage line are each cheap, but most other harnesses expose no quota figure at all, so the inputs are not all visible and the composite cap does not apply - and a pane sweep does not recover quota. Any combined capacity picture therefore leans on estimation for the silent harnesses. Impact prevents a blown window and dead time.
